main_text.p: postrema verba in Cicetonis editionibus nulla sunt: quæ Nonius tamen, vt Ciceronis, adsert.
P. 137. v. 3. Roxanis] Ea etat Oxyattis Bactriani filia. Art. lib. 7. vide Curtium lib. 9.
V. 18. Maternas fordes] Vide Plutarchum exttemo vitæ.5 Alexandri.

V. 30. Arideum Al. fr. regem] Legendus Diod. initio lib. 18. & Curt. lib. 10. Seneca de benef. Quid sibi voluit prouid. nisa, quæ Arrhideum regno imposuit? illi putas hoc datum patri eius datum est, & fratri.10
P. 138. v. 9. Attalus, ad interf.] Mcleagro id tribuit Curt. lib. 10.
32. Corpus Alexandri] Quod ad id tempus infepultū fuerat. Ælian. extr. lib. 12. Alexandria autem deportatum à Ptolemæo, idem auctor est, & Strabo 17. & Diod. 18.15
P. 139. v. 8. Arabiaque pars] Mss. vnum & Orofium lib. 3. cap. 23. expressi. Mss. enim ceteri Asia Libyaque pars.
V. 11. Cleomenes] Dinocrates dicitur Val. Max lib. 1. ca. 5. & Solino. Cleomenes autem Africæ & Ægypti vectigalibus fuerat præpositus. Curt. lib. 4.20

V. 12. Laumedon] Infra lib. 15. Laudice pro Laodice Veteres Latinos Laumento pro Laomedonte dixisse, docuit nos Josephus Scaliger in Festum, quem vide. In 14. Annalium Taciti quæ Boodicea, eadem statim Boudicea dicitur, in vita Agricolæ Voadica, vitiose fortassis: & apud Petronium Laucoon pro Laocoon.25

V. 14. Acropatos] Legendum ex Arriani 7. Atropates li. 6. Ἀτροπάτης. Is Diodoro Ἀτροπάτης mendose, pro Ἀτροπά-της. Diligenter comparandus est hic locus cum principio lib. 18. Diod. Siculi. Videndus & Curtius & Appianus Συεμαχῆ.30

V. 15. Phrygia maior] Omnino emendandum, Phrygia maior Ant. Phil filio assignatur, cum Lycia & Pamphilia: Cariam, &c. ex Diod. App. Curtio. τόπω mutarunt in Nearcho, cum vni tot regiones assignari ægre ferrent: Inue: so inde ordine legerunt, Liciam & Pamphiliam Nearco. Et mihi quidem ita videtur.35
24. Terras inter] Seras edidit in Orofio Fabricius quomodo habet è Mss. nostris vnus: ceteri, Terras quod malo. Nam & vrbs Taxila, cui imperabat Taxiles, siue Taxilus,40

page.notes: Marginal line numbers 5, 10, 15, 20, 25, 30, 35, 40 are reproduced as notes; the printed Greek in V. 14 and V. 15 is transcribed as best read and may contain errors; the lower-right "xilus," is a catchword-like continuation and is left in the text.
